editorial:
Imagine having the perfect life: a big house, a successful lawyer for a husband, and kids who adore you. That is exactly what you see when you first meet Kate. She looks like the ideal suburban mom who has everything under control. But as you get closer to her, you realize there is a dark secret hiding behind her smile. She is struggling with bulimia, and the movie shows how she fights to keep her eating disorder a secret from everyone she loves. It feels like a pressure cooker where the tension builds up as she tries to maintain a fake image while falling apart inside.

The acting is really strong and makes you feel for Kate even when she makes bad choices. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow since it is an older TV movie. If you like dramas that dive into family secrets and mental health, you will find this very moving. Since this is an older gem, you might want to look for it on a digital rental through Apple TV or track down a physical copy for your collection if you like owning your movies. It is a great pick for a quiet night in when you want something with a lot of heart.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Kate can no longer hide her sickness from her family. The secret finally blows up, leading to an emotional confrontation with her husband. Instead of everything falling apart, the ending focuses on the long road to recovery. Kate admits she needs help and starts the hard process of therapy. It wraps up on a hopeful note, showing that honesty is the only way to actually heal and save her marriage.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional family dramas and stories about overcoming personal struggles.
